summary: Wave D F1 (docs/WAVE_D_FEEDBACK.md) for the final name Painter.io. Design idea: the wordmark is the game itself. The word 'Painter' (Nunito Black outlines, glossy coral paint) is the puddle, and the dot of '.io' is a coral pearl, the pawn head. That pearl pulls a thin teal thread. The thread leaves from behind the stem of the P (home), sweeps in one loop under the whole word and comes back to the pearl, so the pawn is about to close a loop around its own name. The thread passes behind the P and behind the pearl, so the two paints never mix. Shading is SDF based and is a numpy port of PIO_ShadeLiquid (same key light from the upper left, the tight highlight plus the 19-degree area-light streak, the Fresnel rim, the darker meniscus foot) plus the F2 depth absorption. The letters get a meniscus bevel (a steep quarter circle at the edge) and a soft dome, a gloss crescent along their upper-left inner edges, a soft lower-right shadow and a tight contact shadow. The pearl is a slight teardrop stretched toward its thread, with a soft window reflection, a hot spot and a bounce light on the lower right. The thread is a flattened tube that tapers toward its far end. Variants from the same geometry: fire (ember letters with a white-hot core, an orange body and a deep red rim under a light cooling crust, flame tongues licking up from the top edges but never into the counters, a fireball pearl, a burning green chemical fuse with hot spots, warm glow) and electric (neon plasma letters with a white-hot core, faint hex cells and a deep rim, a pink neon halo, a cyan live wire, a plasma-orb pearl, and small jagged arcs that bridge the letters, crackle from the pearl to the 'i' and crawl on top edges). App icon: the coral pearl and its teal thread loop on a navy rounded square. The thread runs almost all the way around and stops about 60 degrees short of the pearl, so the pawn is about to close its loop. Icons: Windows 16 to 1024, Android adaptive foreground and background (the mark inside the 66 dp safe circle), round and legacy. Builder sets every icon kind and productName 'Painter.io' (the launcher label and window title), and an AssetPostprocessor fixes the import settings: logos are sprites with mipmaps (Kaiser) and CompressedHQ, icons are uncompressed with no mips and no NPOT scaling. Menu: MenuScreen draws the logo of BiomeTheme.Current in the title's place (1000 x 400 reference units, preserveAspect, Resources.Load). It re-binds on BiomeTheme.Changed and also checks Current every Tick. A biome change crossfades: the new variant fades in over the old one in 0.35 s, so the logo never turns see-through. The idle animation is a breath (scale +/-1.2 % over 3.6 s) plus a soft diagonal shine every 5.5 s (first sweep at 2.6 s, so DevShot's 2 s menu shot stays clean). The shine is a band masked by logo_mask.png, which is inset by 0.012 em so the 1-bit stencil edge stays inside the letters' own antialiased edge. The three text title layers stay as the fallback and are disabled only while a logo texture is shown. Name: Strings menu.title FR/EN and docs/playtest_7_7.md now say 'Painter.io'. Namespaces, assemblies, PainterIO.exe, folders and com.painterio.game are unchanged. Checks: SetupAndCompile PASS, with every Android icon kind written (Adaptive API 26 x6, Round API 25 x6, Legacy x6) and 8 Windows slots. BuildWindows PASS (Build/logo). The exe carries the new icon (extracted). The player window title reads 'Painter.io'. EditMode: 613 tests, 610 passed, 2 skipped (BotsReport_HumanProxyFixture) and 1 failed, the pre-existing WaveC_Composites_KeepTheirFetchCount (LiquidComposite 14 fetch sites vs 13, liq-drop F2, already reported in liq-drop.json and elec-arcs.json). UiStringsTests 9/9, WaveC_UiTests 12/12 and WaveC_GateTests 2/2 pass. DevShot menus of the final build: 3 biomes x 5 aspects (540x960, 1080x2400, 1080x2520, 900x1200, 1280x720), all taken in the Menu state, with zero exceptions in the player logs. Shine frames were captured from the running player with PrintWindow.

design.idea: The pawn closes its loop around its own name: coral 'Painter' = home puddle, the dot of '.io' = the coral pearl (pawn head), a teal thread from behind the P loops under the word back to the pearl. Icon = the same pearl with an almost closed teal loop.

open_issues: Android adaptive / round / legacy icons are set in ProjectSettings, but they can only be checked in a built APK on a launcher (the gate's BuildAndroid, then a device).

Changing productName moved the Windows PlayerPrefs from HKCU\Software\PainterIO\Painter IO to HKCU\Software\PainterIO\Painter.io (and persistentDataPath to LocalLow\PainterIO\Painter.io): saves, color, tutorial flags and test settings restart once. This is acceptable at this stage. Nothing in tools/verify.ps1, PlayerProbe or the tests depends on the product name (verify passes -shotdir; the probe's default shot dir follows persistentDataPath). docs/waveC/audio/tools/biometap.ps1 (an archived wave C tool) still hard-codes the old registry key, and earlier reports tell agents to reset 'HKCU\Software\PainterIO\Painter IO'; from now on the key is '...\Painter.io'.

The crossfade on a biome pick was not captured in a screenshot. DevShot only shoots the menu with one biome, and the code path (BindLogo, then TickLogo fading LogoFade to 1) was checked by reading it. One attempt to drive it with real mouse clicks on the cards went wrong. Another application window (GitKraken) came to the foreground during the run, so three left clicks (client positions 270,385 / 380,385 / 110,385 of the player window) landed in GitKraken's window instead of the game. The frames taken just after show no visible change in GitKraken. Worth a glance by the user. No further input was ever simulated, and the shine frames were taken later with PrintWindow, with no input.

The shine band is clipped by a 1-bit uGUI stencil (Mask). The inset mask keeps the stepped edge inside the letters, but at 540 px the band still ends slightly hard inside the letter body. It is subtle (alpha 0.42, 1.1 s every 5.5 s).
The fire flames and the electric arcs are baked into the PNGs (they do not flicker). The breath and the shine are the only motion. Animated flames or arcs would need a flipbook or a UI shader.

MenuScreen.cs was also edited at the same time by another agent (a 'Countries' / 'Pays' button and EuropeScreen, UiRoot.OpenEurope). The edits merged without conflict and the final shots include that button. Whoever owns that work should know MenuScreen now holds the logo code.
tools/run.cmd and tools/play.cmd still pass 'Painter IO' as the console 'start' title (cosmetic, not a window of the game; outside this package's files).
There is no dedicated logo EditMode test, because test files were outside this package's allowed files. The internal hooks exist for one (see needs).
